 Learn more US stocks were mixed as Americans went to the polls for the midterm elections and braced for more earnings from the AI industry, including chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ). 
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell roughly 0.4%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.4%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) advanced by about 0.8% as chip stocks rebounded following a turbulent day for chip stocks. 
 ( ^DJI )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 51,786.72 -197.26 (-0.38%) At close: 4:34:56 PM EST ^DJI ^GSPC ^IXIC This evening, investors will watch the election results and ballot initiatives for insights into potential policy changes on key issues affecting markets, including pharmaceuticals, the housing market, and AI data centers. 
 But before then, AMD will report earnings after the closing bell, giving investors another glimpse of AI demand at a precarious time for the artificial intelligence trade. As Intel's ( INTC ) stock demonstrated last week , the market's reaction is likely to depend as much on Q4 guidance as on the company's top- and bottom-line results in the most recent quarter. 
 Apple ( AAPL ) stock fell following its own earnings report, which showed several bright spots (iPhone sales) but also some misses (Greater China revenue). Palantir ( PLTR ) stock also fell post-earnings despite results that beat expectations. 
 While earnings season continues apace, the Labor Department released its monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) report, showing openings and hiring  changed little in September,  continuing the labor market's "low hire, low fire" trend. 
 LIVE 18 updates Today at 9:29 PM UTC Ines Ferré AMD beats Q3 estimates, stock soars 7% in after-hours
 Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports: 
 AMD ( AMD ) reported its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, as the company's data center revenue grew 97%. 
 AMD stock climbed more than 7% following the news. 
 "Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement. 
 "With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."

 Today at 9:01 PM UTC Ines Ferré Stocks close session mixed as traders focus on election results, AMD and Supermicro earnings
 Stocks closed the session mixed on Tuesday as investors shifted focus to midterm election results and upcoming earnings from AI players AMD ( AMD ) and Super Micro Computer ( SMCI ). 
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell more than 0.4%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) advanced by almost 0.8% as chip stocks rallied. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) edged up 0.4%. 
 ( AMD )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 483.90 +17.06 (+3.65%) At close: 4:00:02 PM EST 520.99 +37.09 (+7.66%) After hours: 6:11:44 PM EST AMD SMCI The major averages diverged as Americans headed to the polls to vote for congressional seats and state policies across the US. 
 Oil prices trimmed losses by afternoon trading on Tuesday. Brent crude futures ( BZ=F ) dropped less than 1% to hover near $104 per barrel, while WTI ( CL=F ) exchanged hands near $96 per barrel. 
 Today at 8:04 PM UTC Ines Ferré Super Micro to report Q1 earnings as AI trade attempts comeback
 Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reports: 
 Data center infrastructure company Super Micro ( SMCI ) will report its fiscal first-quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, as the AI trade attempts a comeback following sharp declines driven by renewed fears of an AI bubble. 
 Super Micro stock fell a staggering 27% over the last month after Gartner issued a report saying that 80% of neocloud companies would cease operations by 2030 due to a lack of a return on invested capital. 
 Read more here. 
 Today at 7:13 PM UTC David Hollerith Record breaking Binance heist hinged on fake job interview 
 Hackers behind the record-breaking  Binance heist  spent weeks masquerading as recruiters and faux executives, eventually convincing an engineer to download malicious software onto a work computer as part of a larger-scale ruse, the company  said  Tuesday. 
 Binance said the ploy included two rounds of interviews, with a supposed HR representative conducting the first interview and sharing their social media account information to gain trust with the programmer. A second person, posing as the CEO of a fake company, later convinced the engineer to download a file containing malware under the guise of an interview assessment. 
 The fake job interview was just one stage of the hackers' multistep attack. Binance said the campaign began in June when another engineer downloaded a tampered software installer. Additional employee devices were compromised before the hackers gained access to systems involved in authorizing wallet transactions. 
 Over the weekend, the Federal Bureau of Investigation said Democratic People's Republic of Korea was behind the incident. The rogue regime has since denied the allegation. 
 Binance added in the update that it has fended off 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases so far this year. 
 Read more: 
 Today at 6:15 PM UTC Ines Ferré What a Democratic sweep could mean for stocks — and why history says not much
 Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre reports: 
 Polls and prediction markets have spent weeks pointing to a Democratic sweep. History says the outcome has shaped stocks for about three months, then barely at all. 
 That may surprise anyone bracing for a long night of maps and swing counties. Polymarket gave Democrats a 76% chance of winning both the House and the Senate as of Tuesday morning, with a Democratic House and a Republican Senate a distant second at 19%. 
 The House looks like the surer bet. The Senate is where the drama is. Republicans hold it 53-47, Democrats need a net gain of four seats, and polling models and prediction markets differ more on that chamber . Some races may not be called Tuesday night. 
 Read more here. 
 Today at 5:47 PM UTC David Hollerith Bitcoin is "rigged for a major move," says crypto analyst
 The value of the crypto market rose slightly Tuesday to $2.6 trillion, but the industry's near-term direction heading into November looks far from clear. 
 At the end of last week, turmoil erupted in the crypto world after major crypto exchange Binance was hit by a record hack. In the two business days following the Binance hack last Thursday, investors pulled over $1 billion from US-listed bitcoin exchange-traded products, according to Bloomberg data . 
 Bitcoin was down more than 3% as of noon ET, hovering around $77,600. Signals in the crypto derivatives market are also flashing a clear split signal, according to Norway-based crypto brokerage K33. Open interest on CME bitcoin futures has fallen to its lowest level since October 2023. Meanwhile, open interest in perpetual futures tied to bitcoin is positioned at a three-month high. 
 No matter what the outcome of US midterm elections, bitcoin is "rigged for a major move," K33 head of research Vetle Lunde told clients Tuesday. 
 Today at 4:49 PM UTC Ines Ferré Oil falls for second day in a row on hopes of Middle East talks
 Oil prices dropped for a second day in a row on Tuesday as investors priced in the odds of a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict. 
 Brent crude oil futures ( BZ=F ) tumbled 1% to hover near $103 per barrel, while WTI ( CL=F ) also fell to trade near $95 per barrel amid hopes of peace talks in the Iran-US conflict. 
 The declines come a day after futures plummeted 7% as both the US and Iran signaled a preference for talks in the Middle East. 
 Today at 3:59 PM UTC David Hollerith Job openings and hiring edged higher in September, but it's still a 'low hire, low fire' market
 Job openings and hiring changed little in September, the Labor Department's monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey showed, as the "low hire, low fire" labor market continued, Yahoo Finance's Claire Boston reports: 
 There were 7.5 million job openings in September, from a revised 7.2 million a month earlier, the report showed. The hiring rate improved slightly to 3.4%, up from 3.3% in September. 
 A fuller look at the job market will be released on Friday, when the Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes its monthly payrolls report for October. 
 Read more: 
 Today at 3:37 PM UTC David Hollerith Chip stocks are bouncing back from a fresh bear market as Wall Street's safe havens slip
 Monday's close left chip stocks in a fresh bear market, below their summer lows and a key technical level. Tuesday, they're bouncing back like they want to make the bears regret it, Yahoo Finance Jared Blikre reports: 
 The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) finished Nov. 2 about 22% below its Oct. 6 high, its second bear market since June. It was also the index's second straight close below its 200-day moving average , a line it hadn't closed under since June 2025, and its lowest close since April. 
 Nearly every chip and storage stock in the S&P 500 rose in early trading Tuesday, led by memory and chip-equipment names, and the index climbed back above its July 29 low. If chips can hold that ground, Monday's breakdown starts to look like a bear trap — a break below a key level that quickly reverses, catching traders who bet on more losses. 
 Read more: 
 Today at 3:30 PM UTC David Hollerith CrowdStrike says it will buy two AI cybersecurity startups. Shares rise. 
 CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) said Tuesday that it has agreed to buy two AI security startups, Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré reports: 
 CrowdStrike said it has signed an agreement to acquire Fiddler AI, a startup that develops tools that help companies track their AI systems. 
 The company also announced an agreement to acquire Dreadnode, a startup that develops tools to test AI systems for security vulnerabilities. CrowdStrike said the technology will allow its Falcon platform to continuously scan AI models, applications, and agents for potential security weaknesses before they are deployed. 
 The combined purchase price for both is $495 million , according to the Wall Street Journal. Shares of the cybersecurity company gained more than 2% in early trading. 
 Read more: 
 Today at 3:02 PM UTC Brooke DiPalma Gas and diesel prices hit record Election Day highs 
 Gas and diesel prices are the highest they have ever been on any Election Day in US history, according to Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy head of petroleum analysis. 
 The national average price for a gallon of gasoline is now $4.14, while a gallon of diesel is $6.29, according to  AAA . 
 Higher prices, especially for fuel, are a key source of voter frustration heading into the polls on Tuesday. 
 Futures on Brent crude ( BZ=F ), the international benchmark, fell roughly 1% to trade around $104 per barrel Tuesday morning, whereas US WTI crude ( CL=F ) broke the $100 mark on Monday and is now trading around $96, down 6% from five days ago. 
 Brent crude ended October at a six-month high amid concerns that the conflict will reescalate following the midterm elections. The pullback from that peak comes as hopes return to the market over talks of a potential ceasefire between the US and Iran. 
 Today at 2:36 PM UTC David Hollerith US stocks mixed as midterm results loom
 US stocks opened mixed Tuesday as investors awaited midterm election results and more AI-related earnings to come. 
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.4%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) advanced by 0.3% following a turbulent day for chip stocks. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) was up slightly. 
 ( ^DJI )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 51,786.72 -197.26 (-0.38%) At close: 4:34:56 PM EST ^DJI ^GSPC ^IXIC Investors will watch election results Tuesday evening for potential shifts in policy around areas including housing, pharmaceuticals, and AI infrastructure. Before then, Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) reports after the bell, offering another read on AI demand after a sharp sell-off in chip stocks. 
 Apple ( AAPL ) and Palantir ( PLTR ) also traded lower following their earnings reports, along with pharmaceutical maker Pfizer ( PFE ) and e-commerce platform Shopify ( SHOP ). 
 Today at 2:05 PM UTC Ines Ferré Shopify stock tanks as Q3 revenue, total order value miss Wall Street estimates
 Shopify ( SHOP ) stock plunged 15% in premarket trading on Tuesday after reporting third quarter results that missed the mark on several key metrics. 
 The cloud-based e-commerce platform's Q3 revenue of $3.74 billion came in just shy of consensus estimates of $3.75 billion for the first time since 2022, according to Bloomberg data. Subscription revenue for the quarter of $836 million also missed Wall Street expectations of $850.2 million, raising concerns about growth in its main recurring-revenue business. 
 Gross merchandise volume, or the total dollar value of orders sold through Shopify's platform, was $119.15 billion, also falling short of estimates of $120.08 billion. 
 Shopify's adjusted earnings per share of $0.49 topped estimates of $0.48. 
 Read more. 
 Today at 12:32 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Binance co-founder CZ says users 'did not suffer any loss' after $6.3B hack
 Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi sat down with Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, better known in crypto circles as CZ , after hackers took roughly $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency trading platform . 
 "It's been a pretty hectic process," Zhao said of the aftermath of the hack. "But the good thing is right now the withdrawals have been restored, the systems back to normal. People are free to use the platform without any issues now. And then all user funds are covered. The users did not suffer any loss." 
 Sozzi writes that Binance moved swiftly to stabilize the situation by guaranteeing full customer restitution, deploying corporate treasury reserves, Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) capital, and insurance funds to replenish user balances. 
 "There's no 100% security," CZ added. "So when you run a platform, especially a crypto platform the possibility is always there. I did not think it was going to be this big of magnitude, probably not." 
 Today at 12:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Prediction markets vs. polls: Election forecasting industry faces midterm test
 Yahoo Finance's Ben Werschkul reports: 
 Prediction markets and pollsters both say Democrats are favored to take both the US House and Senate on Tuesday. But prediction markets are a little less certain about it, especially on the Senate side. 
 That's setting up what could be another chapter in the burgeoning rivalry between prediction markets and polls following 2024's closely watched results. The upper chamber is where the differences are most evident.  
 A small but consistent gap has been evident for months in the odds of Democrats taking control of the Senate. The gap has averaged about 7.4 percentage points since Sept. 1, according to a Yahoo Finance analysis 
 It sat at 7.2 percentage points on Monday, with three prediction markets placing a 73.1% chance of Democrats taking control while two polling-based models suggested the chances are higher at 80.3%.

 Today at 11:01 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Apple showed once again that consumers will complain — but still tap to pay
 Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban writes for today's Morning Brief newsletter: 
 It's not easy forking over more than $1,000 for a new iPhone every couple of years. But Apple ( AAPL ) has proved yet again that complaining about prices isn't the same thing as being unwilling to make the purchase. 
 The company reported its quarter on Monday after the bell, posting revenue that grew 12% last quarter and beating Wall Street's expectations. The company also beat on earnings per share. 
 Apple's muscular iPhone sales are a microcosm of one of the major forces that have powered the economy. Though people may be furious with rising prices, the indefatigable American consumer continues to tap-to-pay through the rage.

 Today at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Some highlights from Palantir's earnings call on Monday night
 Palantir's ( PLTR ) third quarter revenue and profits beat Wall Street estimates , and the company raised its full-year revenue outlook, Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré reported on Monday. 
 In another milestone, the company's US commercial business surpassed its US government sales for the first time ever. 
 "We've gone from being the most attractive person in the physics department to being the captain of the football team," Palantir CEO Alex Karp said during the earnings call.
